- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. - anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

31

Group Meetups: Feature Spec

32

First Epic Workflow Challenge - Senior Full-Stack Engineer (ALTAIR). Original First Epic material built for this workflow challenge. All names, places, and coordinates are synthetic.

33 34
This spec covers one defined slice of a community app: group meetups, RSVPs, and the meetup map. It is not an invitation to build the whole app. You also receive a schema starter (altair-schema-starter) and seed data (altair-seed-data.sql). If anything here is ambiguous, state your assumption in your note and proceed.
35 36

1. Background

37

Members of the app belong to small neighborhood walking groups. A group is a handful to a few dozen neighbors who walk together. Today members coordinate walks in side channels. This feature lets any member post a meetup to their group, lets other members RSVP, and shows where to meet on a map.

38 39

2. Who is involved

40
41 42 43 44 45 46
RoleWho
Group memberA user with a row in group_memberships for that group. A user can belong to several groups.
CreatorThe group member who created a given meetup.
AttendeeA group member who has RSVP'd to a given meetup.
OutsiderAny signed-in user who is not a member of the meetup's group.
47

Every request comes from a signed-in user. Anonymous access to anything in this feature is out of scope and should be denied. The app signs in with the seeded test accounts (email and password, listed in section 13); no sign-up flow is needed.

48 49

Target platform

50
    51
  • One platform is enough: iOS or Android, on a simulator, an emulator, a device, or Expo Go. Pick whichever you can run.
    • 52
  • The web client is out of scope for this slice.
    • 53
  • The provided database starter is designed to boot (database up, seed loaded, a seed account signed in) in under 30 minutes once Docker (or a hosted Supabase project) is ready. If it takes you longer, say what slowed you down in your note.
    • 54
55 56

3. What already exists

57

The schema starter gives you users (one profile per account, including a private home location), groups, and group_memberships (many-to-many). Row-level security is switched on for those three tables with no policies. There are no meetup or RSVP tables, no policies, and no endpoints. The supabase/migrations folder is empty.

58 59

4. Meetups

60

Fields

61
62 63 64 65 66 67 68 69
FieldRule
GroupRequired. The creator must be a member of it.
TitleRequired, 1 to 80 characters after trimming.
Start timeRequired, stored with time zone. Must be in the future when the meetup is created; the server rejects a past or current start time.
Meeting pointRequired: a place name (1 to 120 characters, for example "North gate, Linden Park") and a latitude and longitude in valid ranges. Meeting points are public places.
CreatorSet by the server from the signed-in user, never taken from the request body.
StatusScheduled or cancelled.
70

Behavior

71
    72
  • Any member of a group can create a meetup in that group.
    • 73
  • Members of the group can list the group's meetups, soonest first, and open a meetup's detail.
    • 74
  • Only the creator can cancel a meetup. Cancel is required: build it, enforce creator-only on the server, and cover it in your tests.
    • 75
76

Cancelled meetups

77
    78
  • A cancelled meetup stays visible to its group, clearly marked as cancelled, in the list and on the detail.
    • 79
  • It accepts no new RSVPs. Existing attendees stay listed, and a member can still withdraw their own RSVP.
    • 80
  • Cancelling is final: a cancelled meetup cannot be reopened.
    • 81
  • Outsiders still see nothing about it.
    • 82
83

Bonus: editing a meetup (optional)

84

Letting the creator edit a meetup (title, start time, meeting point) is optional and never held against you if skipped. If you build it: creator-only on the server, a changed start time must still be in the future, a cancelled meetup cannot be edited, and cover it in your tests.

85 86

My groups

87

The app needs to know which groups the signed-in member belongs to, to choose a group's meetup list. A read-only "my groups" endpoint or query is expected: it returns only the caller's own groups. Creating or managing groups is out of scope.

88 89

5. RSVPs

90
    91
  • A member of the meetup's group can RSVP to it, and can cancel their own RSVP.
    • 92
  • One RSVP per member per meetup. RSVPing twice is not an error the user should see; it leaves one RSVP.
    • 93
  • No RSVPs to a cancelled meetup or one that has already started.
    • 94
  • To test a started meetup, your test setup may insert or update one directly as the database owner.
    • 95
  • A member can only RSVP, or cancel an RSVP, for themselves.
    • 96
  • The meetup detail shows the attendee list: the display names of members who have RSVP'd.
    • 97
98 99

6. Who sees what

100
101 102 103 104 105 106
Meetup (title, time, status)Attendee listMeeting pointCancel
OutsiderNoNoNoNo
Group member, not RSVP'dYesYesOpen decision (section 7)No
Group member, RSVP'dYesYesExactNo
CreatorYesYesExactYes
107

Edit (bonus, if built) follows the same rule as cancel: creator only.

108

"No" means the data never leaves the server for that user: not in a list, a detail, an attendee query, a map payload, or an error message. Access must be enforced in the database or on the server, never by hiding data in the app after it arrives.

109

A member of several groups sees each group's meetups according to their own status in that meetup. An RSVP to one meetup grants nothing for any other meetup.

110 111

7. The open product decision

112
113

Should group members who have not RSVP'd see the exact meeting point, or only an approximate area until they RSVP?

114

This is left open on purpose. Make the call, build it, and explain it in your note with a reason grounded in the people using the app. Whichever you choose:

115
    116
  • It is enforced in the database or on the server. If you choose the approximate area, the exact coordinates never reach the app for a member who has not RSVP'd, and neither does anything else that pins down the exact spot.
    • 117
  • Place name: the meeting point's place name (for example "North gate, Linden Park") pins down the spot as precisely as coordinates do. Under the approximate area it is withheld until RSVP, like the exact coordinates; you may show a coarse label of your own instead. Under the exact choice it is shown.
    • 118
  • If you choose the approximate area, it means this: an area computed on the server (or in the database), with a radius of at least 300 meters, whose center is NOT the exact point (for example snapped to a grid cell, or offset by a fixed amount stored per meetup). The exact coordinates never reach the client before the member RSVPs. Within those rules, how you compute it and how large you make it is your call; say why in your note.
    • 119
  • Once a member RSVPs, their view of the meeting point updates to what an attendee sees, without reinstalling or signing out.
    • 120
121
122 123

8. Home location privacy rule

124

Each user's profile holds a home location (users.home_lat, users.home_lng), collected for features outside this slice. It is private.

125
    126
  • No home location may appear in any response from this feature, for any user: no endpoint, view, function, attendee list, map payload, or error.
    • 127
  • No home location may appear on the map, as a marker, an area, or a starting point.
    • 128
  • Do not build anything in this slice that is derived from a home location (for example, distance from home).
    • 129
130 131

9. App screens and map

132

Minimal app UI (required)

133
    134
  • Sign in with a seed account (Supabase Auth, directly from the app).
    • 135
  • Meetup list for a group, with loading, empty, and error states. Choose the group any simple way (for example a picker fed by the "my groups" query, or the member's first group); a dedicated groups screen is not required.
    • 136
  • Create meetup screen: title, start time, meeting point (place name plus a point, picked on the map or entered as coordinates), with server errors shown to the user.
    • 137
  • Meetup detail: title, time, status, attendee list, the map, an RSVP action, and a cancel action shown only to the creator.
    • 138
139

Withdrawing an RSVP needs its endpoint and a test; a withdraw button in the app is optional. Plain, functional screens are enough; visual polish is not graded. An edit screen belongs to the optional edit bonus.

140

Map

141
    142
  • On the meetup detail, show the meeting point on a map. Any map option is fine. A path that needs no account and no card exists: react-native-maps with the platform's default map, which runs in Expo Go and on the iOS simulator or an Android emulator.
    • 143
  • Render whatever the server says this member may see: an exact point, or the approximate area you designed.
    • 144
  • After the member RSVPs, the map shows the attendee view.
    • 145
  • Handle loading, empty, and error states.
    • 146
147 148

10. One shared contract

149

Request and response shapes for creating and cancelling a meetup, listing a group's meetups, listing my groups, and RSVPing or withdrawing an RSVP (and editing, if you build the bonus) live as Zod schemas in one shared place that both the endpoints and the React Native app import.

150
    151
  • Writes: every write (create a meetup, RSVP, withdraw an RSVP, cancel a meetup, and edit if you build the bonus) goes through an endpoint layer that validates it on the server with those shared Zod schemas: a Supabase Edge Function or a small TypeScript server, your choice. Postgres functions are fine behind that layer, called by your endpoint code; a write sent from the app straight to a table or a Postgres function does not meet the requirement, and SQL checks alone do not meet the Zod-validated requirement.
    • 152
  • Reads: lists, my groups, meetup detail, and map data may be queried directly from the app with the member's session under row-level security, or go through your endpoints. Either way, the visibility rules in sections 6 to 8 hold.
    • 153
  • Sign-in: the app signs in with Supabase Auth directly.
    • 154
  • The server rejects invalid input with a clear error, whatever the app does.
    • 155
156 157

11. Run instructions

158

Include short run instructions with your submission: how a reviewer starts the database, loads the seed, runs the endpoints and the app, and runs your tests, from a clean checkout. A reviewer will follow them as written.

159 160

12. Out of scope

161
    162
  • Sign-up and account flows beyond signing in with the seed accounts.
    • 163
  • The web client.
    • 164
  • Creating or managing groups and memberships.
    • 165
  • Notifications, chat, comments, recurring meetups, and invitations.
    • 166
  • Live location sharing (that is the optional bonus in the brief, not part of the required slice).
    • 167
  • Editing profiles or home locations.
    • 168
169 170

13. Seed cast

171

The seed data signs every account in with password altair-fixture-pass.

172
173 174 175 176 177 178 179 180 181 182
MemberGroupsRole in the reference meetups

183 184

Reference meetups (seed PART 2)

185

MeetupGroupStartMeeting pointRSVPs
Saturday morning loopMaple Street Walkers7 days after the seed is loadedNorth gate, Linden Park (40.012046, -99.984517)Jordan Price, Riley Chen

A member of several groups sees each group's meetups according to their own status in that meetup. An RSVP to one meetup grants nothing for any other meetup.

7. The open product decision

Should group members who have not RSVP'd see the exact meeting point, or only an approximate area until they RSVP?

This is left open on purpose. Make the call, build it, and explain it in your note with a reason grounded in the people using the app. Whichever you choose:

  • It is enforced in the database or on the server. If you choose the approximate area, the exact coordinates never reach the app for a member who has not RSVP'd, and neither does anything else that pins down the exact spot.
  • Place name: the meeting point's place name (for example "North gate, Linden Park") pins down the spot as precisely as coordinates do. Under the approximate area it is withheld until RSVP, like the exact coordinates; you may show a coarse label of your own instead. Under the exact choice it is shown.
  • If you choose the approximate area, it means this: an area computed on the server (or in the database), with a radius of at least 300 meters, whose center is NOT the exact point (for example snapped to a grid cell, or offset by a fixed amount stored per meetup). The exact coordinates never reach the client before the member RSVPs. Within those rules, how you compute it and how large you make it is your call; say why in your note.
  • Once a member RSVPs, their view of the meeting point updates to what an attendee sees, without reinstalling or signing out.

8. Home location privacy rule

Each user's profile holds a home location (users.home_lat, users.home_lng), collected for features outside this slice. It is private.

  • No home location may appear in any response from this feature, for any user: no endpoint, view, function, attendee list, map payload, or error.
  • No home location may appear on the map, as a marker, an area, or a starting point.
  • Do not build anything in this slice that is derived from a home location (for example, distance from home).

9. App screens and map

Minimal app UI (required)

  • Sign in with a seed account (Supabase Auth, directly from the app).
  • Meetup list for a group, with loading, empty, and error states. Choose the group any simple way (for example a picker fed by the "my groups" query, or the member's first group); a dedicated groups screen is not required.
  • Create meetup screen: title, start time, meeting point (place name plus a point, picked on the map or entered as coordinates), with server errors shown to the user.
  • Meetup detail: title, time, status, attendee list, the map, an RSVP action, and a cancel action shown only to the creator.

Withdrawing an RSVP needs its endpoint and a test; a withdraw button in the app is optional. Plain, functional screens are enough; visual polish is not graded. An edit screen belongs to the optional edit bonus.

Map

  • On the meetup detail, show the meeting point on a map. Any map option is fine. A path that needs no account and no card exists: react-native-maps with the platform's default map, which runs in Expo Go and on the iOS simulator or an Android emulator.
  • Render whatever the server says this member may see: an exact point, or the approximate area you designed.
  • After the member RSVPs, the map shows the attendee view.
  • Handle loading, empty, and error states.

10. One shared contract

Request and response shapes for creating and cancelling a meetup, listing a group's meetups, listing my groups, and RSVPing or withdrawing an RSVP (and editing, if you build the bonus) live as Zod schemas in one shared place that both the endpoints and the React Native app import.

  • Writes: every write (create a meetup, RSVP, withdraw an RSVP, cancel a meetup, and edit if you build the bonus) goes through an endpoint layer that validates it on the server with those shared Zod schemas: a Supabase Edge Function or a small TypeScript server, your choice. Postgres functions are fine behind that layer, called by your endpoint code; a write sent from the app straight to a table or a Postgres function does not meet the requirement, and SQL checks alone do not meet the Zod-validated requirement.
  • Reads: lists, my groups, meetup detail, and map data may be queried directly from the app with the member's session under row-level security, or go through your endpoints. Either way, the visibility rules in sections 6 to 8 hold.
  • Sign-in: the app signs in with Supabase Auth directly.
  • The server rejects invalid input with a clear error, whatever the app does.

11. Run instructions

Include short run instructions with your submission: how a reviewer starts the database, loads the seed, runs the endpoints and the app, and runs your tests, from a clean checkout. A reviewer will follow them as written.

12. Out of scope

  • Sign-up and account flows beyond signing in with the seed accounts.
  • The web client.
  • Creating or managing groups and memberships.
  • Notifications, chat, comments, recurring meetups, and invitations.
  • Live location sharing (that is the optional bonus in the brief, not part of the required slice).
  • Editing profiles or home locations.

-- =====================================================================
-- First Epic Workflow Challenge - Senior Full-Stack Engineer
-- Schema starter (ALTAIR)
--
-- Original First Epic material built for this workflow challenge. Synthetic.
-- Target: Supabase (Postgres 15+). Uses the Supabase auth schema
-- (auth.users) that every Supabase project already has.
--
-- What this file gives you:
--   public.users              one app profile row per auth.users account
--   public.groups             neighborhood walking groups
--   public.group_memberships  many-to-many: which users belong to which groups
--
-- What this file does NOT give you (that is your work):
--   * meetup and RSVP tables
--   * any row-level security policies (RLS is switched on below for the
--     three starter tables, with no policies, so they deny by default)
--   * any views, functions, or endpoints
--
-- Apply it once, before your own migrations (see README.md).
-- =====================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- users: the app profile for each signed-up account
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.users (
  id            uuid primary key references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  display_name  text not null
                check (char_length(display_name) between 1 and 60),

  -- PRIVATE. A member's home location. Collected at onboarding for other
  -- features that are out of scope here. It must never be exposed through
  -- the meetup feature: not in any response, view, or map, to anyone.
  home_lat      double precision
                check (home_lat between -90 and 90),
  home_lng      double precision
                check (home_lng between -180 and 180),

  created_at    timestamptz not null default now()
);

comment on column public.users.home_lat is
  'PRIVATE home latitude. Never expose through the meetup feature.';
comment on column public.users.home_lng is
  'PRIVATE home longitude. Never expose through the meetup feature.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- groups: small neighborhood walking groups
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.groups (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name        text not null
              check (char_length(name) between 1 and 80),
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- group_memberships: many-to-many between users and groups
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.group_memberships (
  group_id    uuid not null references public.groups (id) on delete cascade,
  user_id     uuid not null references public.users (id) on delete cascade,
  joined_at   timestamptz not null default now(),
  primary key (group_id, user_id)
);

create index group_memberships_user_id_idx
  on public.group_memberships (user_id);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Row-level security: ON, with no policies. Deny by default.
-- Write the policies (or other server-side access) your slice needs.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
alter table public.users             enable row level security;
alter table public.groups            enable row level security;
alter table public.group_memberships enable row level security;

Implement the ALTAIR project using a modular, feature-based Clean Architecture.

Follow SOLID principles where appropriate, separation of concerns, dependency inversion, and maintainable TypeScript practices.

Separate presentation, application/business logic, and infrastructure responsibilities.

Use TypeScript strict mode and clearly defined interfaces.

Avoid circular dependencies and unnecessary abstractions.

Design components and services to be independently testable.

Keep configuration and environment-specific values separate from business logic.

Use reusable UI components and a consistent design system.

Do not introduce microservices, excessive design patterns, or complicated abstractions for this small application.

Presentation Layer
→ Application Layer
→ Domain Interfaces
← Infrastructure Implementations

Keep business rules independent of UI frameworks wherever practical.

Separation of concerns

Dependency direction

Module boundaries

Code duplication

Reusability

Maintainability

Type safety

Security boundaries

Unnecessary complexity

MANDATORY: ALTAIR STARTER README COMPLIANCE

Follow the original ALTAIR schema starter README exactly.

These requirements take priority over generic setup recommendations.

1. Database Setup

Use hosted Supabase PostgreSQL as the primary environment.

Do not install or configure Docker unless explicitly requested.

Do not mix local Supabase and hosted Supabase setup procedures.

Choose one consistent database migration workflow.

Prefer Supabase CLI migrations linked to the hosted project so database changes remain reproducible and version-controlled.

If the starter schema has already been applied manually through the SQL Editor, inspect the existing database and migration history before proceeding.

Never blindly apply the starter schema twice.

Never reset or delete an existing hosted database without explicit approval.

2. Starter Database

Use the provided:

altair-schema-starter.sql

altair-seed-data.sql

altair-feature-spec.html

Challenge brief

Do not replace the starter schema with a newly invented schema.

Preserve the original tables and relationships.

Create new timestamped migrations for additional functionality.

Ensure the starter migration executes before all custom migrations.

3. Seed Data

Seed PART 1 creates authentication accounts and initial database records.

It must execute with the necessary database-owner privileges.

After creating the meetups and RSVPs tables, adapt and load seed PART 2.

Do not load PART 2 before the required tables exist.

Verify that the sample users can authenticate successfully.

The seeded accounts use the email format:

<firstname>@example.test

The provided fixture password is:

altair-fixture-pass

These credentials are exclusively for development and testing.

Do not use them as production credentials.

4. Database Startup Verification

The starter environment is designed to boot in under 30 minutes once Docker or hosted Supabase is ready.

Aim to meet this target.

If setup takes longer, document the cause in ENGINEERING_NOTES.md.

Verify:

Database connectivity

Starter tables

Seed records

Authentication

Group memberships

Migration status

Do not proceed with dependent features until database setup is verified.

5. React Native and Expo

Use Expo React Native.

Support at least one working platform:

Android emulator

iOS simulator

Physical Android/iOS device

Expo Go

A web application is not required.

For local backend URLs:

Android emulator may use 10.0.2.2 to access the host machine.

Physical devices should use a reachable LAN IP.

Do not assume 127.0.0.1 on a device refers to the development computer.

For hosted Supabase, use the project's HTTPS API URL.

Never place the Supabase service-role key in the mobile application.

6. Shared Zod Schemas

Keep shared Zod schemas in one package or folder.

Both the backend and React Native application must import the same schemas.

Use one compatible Zod major version.

Ensure Expo Metro resolves shared workspace imports correctly.

If required, configure metro.config.js and watchFolders.

Verify that shared imports work in the actual React Native development environment.

7. Server-Side Write Endpoints

All writes must pass through server-side TypeScript endpoints.

This includes:

Creating meetups

Creating RSVPs

Withdrawing RSVPs

Cancelling meetups

Editing meetups, only if the optional bonus is implemented

Every write must be validated using the shared Zod schemas.

Do not allow the React Native application to write directly to protected tables or call PostgreSQL write functions directly.

PostgreSQL functions may be used internally behind the validated endpoint layer.

Reads may use authenticated Supabase queries under RLS or backend endpoints.

Authentication must use Supabase Auth directly.

8. Map Configuration

Use react-native-maps with the platform's default map provider unless another option is justified.

Avoid unnecessary paid map services or API-key requirements.

The provided seed coordinates are synthetic and represent fictional locations.

Do not assume the displayed real-world map labels correspond to the fictional meeting-point names.

Do not substitute real addresses for the provided reference locations.

Keep any map-related API tokens outside the repository.

9. Final Compliance Audit

After development, perform a dedicated audit against the original README.

Check every setup instruction individually.

For each requirement, record:

Requirement description

Implementation location

Verification method

Actual result

PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, or NOT IMPLEMENTED

Resolve confirmed issues before final submission.

Do not mark a requirement as PASS unless it has been verified.

The original challenge specification and starter README are authoritative if any generated implementation plan conflicts with them.
</pasted_content id="a4f1">

-- =====================================================================
-- Meetups, exact meeting points, and RSVPs.
--
-- Design note: the exact meeting point (place name + coordinates) lives in
-- its own table, public.meetup_meeting_points, instead of on public.meetups.
-- Row-level security is per row, not per column, so splitting the table is
-- what lets RLS alone decide who may read the exact spot. public.meetups
-- only carries the approximate area (a randomly offset circle computed once
-- in the database, see the next migration), which every group member may see.
-- =====================================================================

-- Private schema for helpers. It is not in the Data API's exposed schemas,
-- so nothing here is callable over PostgREST.
create schema if not exists app;
comment on schema app is
  'Private helpers for the meetup slice. Not exposed through the Supabase Data API.';
revoke all on schema app from public;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- meetups
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.meetups (
  id               uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  group_id         uuid not null references public.groups (id) on delete cascade,
  created_by       uuid not null references public.users (id) on delete cascade,
  title            text not null
                   check (title = btrim(title) and char_length(title) between 1 and 80),
  starts_at        timestamptz not null,
  status           text not null default 'scheduled'
                   check (status in ('scheduled', 'cancelled')),
  cancelled_at     timestamptz,

  -- Approximate area shown to members who have not RSVP'd. Never the exact
  -- point: the center is offset from it (see app.approximate_area).
  area_center_lat  double precision not null check (area_center_lat between -90 and 90),
  area_center_lng  double precision not null check (area_center_lng between -180 and 180),
  area_radius_m    integer not null check (area_radius_m >= 300),

  created_at       timestamptz not null default now(),

  constraint meetups_cancelled_at_matches_status
    check ((status = 'cancelled') = (cancelled_at is not null))
);

comment on table public.meetups is
  'Group meetups. Exact meeting point is in meetup_meeting_points (RLS: creator and attendees only).';

-- List query: a group''s meetups ordered by start time.
create index meetups_group_id_starts_at_idx on public.meetups (group_id, starts_at);
create index meetups_created_by_idx on public.meetups (created_by);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- meetup_meeting_points: the EXACT meeting point, one row per meetup
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.meetup_meeting_points (
  meetup_id   uuid primary key references public.meetups (id) on delete cascade,
  place_name  text not null
              check (place_name = btrim(place_name) and char_length(place_name) between 1 and 120),
  latitude    double precision not null check (latitude between -90 and 90),
  longitude   double precision not null check (longitude between -180 and 180)
);

comment on table public.meetup_meeting_points is
  'EXACT meeting point. Readable only by the meetup creator and members who have RSVP''d.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- rsvps: one per member per meetup
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.rsvps (
  meetup_id   uuid not null references public.meetups (id) on delete cascade,
  user_id     uuid not null references public.users (id) on delete cascade,
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  primary key (meetup_id, user_id)
);

create index rsvps_user_id_idx on public.rsvps (user_id);

alter table public.meetups               enable row level security;
alter table public.meetup_meeting_points enable row level security;
alter table public.rsvps                 enable row level security;

-- =====================================================================
-- Access control: grants + row-level security for the meetup slice.
--
-- Two database roles act on behalf of a signed-in member:
--
--   authenticated       Supabase's role for requests carrying a member's
--                       JWT (the app, or the API server's read path).
--                       READ ONLY in this slice: no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
--                       grant on any table, so a write sent from the app
--                       straight to PostgREST is refused by the database.
--
--   altair_api_writer   NOLOGIN role that only the API server can assume
--                       (SET LOCAL ROLE inside a transaction, after it has
--                       verified the member's JWT and validated the body
--                       with the shared Zod schemas). PostgREST cannot
--                       switch to it: it is not granted to `authenticator`.
--                       It holds the minimum write grants, and RLS still
--                       applies to it as the member (creator-only cancel,
--                       own-RSVP-only, members-only create).
--
-- The member's identity comes from the `sub` claim of request.jwt.claims,
-- which PostgREST sets for `authenticated` and the API server sets for
-- `altair_api_writer` from the verified token. app.current_user_id() reads
-- it the same way auth.uid() does; it lives in `app` so the writer role
-- does not need privileges on Supabase's `auth` schema.
-- =====================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Writer role
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
do $$
begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = 'altair_api_writer') then
    create role altair_api_writer nologin noinherit;
  end if;
end
$$;

comment on role altair_api_writer is
  'Assumed only by the ALTAIR API server (SET LOCAL ROLE) for validated writes. Not reachable via PostgREST.';

-- The migration runs as the database owner (postgres), which is also the
-- role the API server connects as; it must be able to SET ROLE to the writer.
grant altair_api_writer to current_user;

grant usage on schema public to altair_api_writer;
grant usage on schema app to authenticated, altair_api_writer;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Identity + membership helpers
-- SECURITY DEFINER predicates read group_memberships without recursing
-- into its own RLS. Each answers a yes/no question about the caller only.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
create function app.current_user_id()
returns uuid
language sql
stable
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select coalesce(
    nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claim.sub', true), ''),
    nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), '')::jsonb ->> 'sub'
  )::uuid
$$;

create function app.is_group_member(p_group_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1 from public.group_memberships gm
     where gm.group_id = p_group_id
       and gm.user_id  = app.current_user_id()
  )
$$;

create function app.is_meetup_member(p_meetup_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1
      from public.meetups m
      join public.group_memberships gm on gm.group_id = m.group_id
     where m.id = p_meetup_id
       and gm.user_id = app.current_user_id()
  )
$$;

-- Creator or attendee, AND still a member of the meetup's group.
-- An RSVP grants exact access to that one meetup only.
create function app.can_see_exact_meeting_point(p_meetup_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1
      from public.meetups m
      join public.group_memberships gm
        on gm.group_id = m.group_id and gm.user_id = app.current_user_id()
     where m.id = p_meetup_id
       and (
         m.created_by = app.current_user_id()
         or exists (
           select 1 from public.rsvps r
            where r.meetup_id = m.id and r.user_id = app.current_user_id()
         )
       )
  )
$$;

create function app.shares_group_with(p_user_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1
      from public.group_memberships mine
      join public.group_memberships theirs on theirs.group_id = mine.group_id
     where mine.user_id   = app.current_user_id()
       and theirs.user_id = p_user_id
  )
$$;

revoke all on function app.current_user_id() from public;
revoke all on function app.is_group_member(uuid) from public;
revoke all on function app.is_meetup_member(uuid) from public;
revoke all on function app.can_see_exact_meeting_point(uuid) from public;
revoke all on function app.shares_group_with(uuid) from public;

grant execute on function app.current_user_id()                   to authenticated, altair_api_writer;
grant execute on function app.is_group_member(uuid)               to authenticated, altair_api_writer;
grant execute on function app.is_meetup_member(uuid)              to authenticated, altair_api_writer;
grant execute on function app.can_see_exact_meeting_point(uuid)   to authenticated, altair_api_writer;
grant execute on function app.shares_group_with(uuid)             to authenticated, altair_api_writer;

grant execute on function app.approximate_area(double precision, double precision) to altair_api_writer;
grant execute on function app.insert_meetup(uuid, uuid, text, timestamptz, text, double precision, double precision, uuid)
  to altair_api_writer;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table privileges. Supabase's default privileges grant ALL on new public
-- tables to anon and authenticated; start from nothing and add back only
-- what this slice needs. anon gets nothing at all.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
revoke all on table public.users                 from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on table public.groups                from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on table public.group_memberships     from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on table public.meetups               from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on table public.meetup_meeting_points from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on table public.rsvps                 from anon, authenticated;

-- users: COLUMN-level grant. home_lat / home_lng are not granted to any
-- client-facing role, so `select home_lat ...` (or `select *`) fails with
-- "permission denied" no matter which rows RLS would allow.
grant select (id, display_name) on table public.users to authenticated, altair_api_writer;

grant select on table public.groups                to authenticated, altair_api_writer;
grant select on table public.group_memberships     to authenticated, altair_api_writer;
grant select on table public.meetups               to authenticated, altair_api_writer;
grant select on table public.meetup_meeting_points to authenticated, altair_api_writer;
grant select on table public.rsvps                 to authenticated, altair_api_writer;

-- Writer: create meetups (+ exact point), cancel (status only), RSVP, withdraw.
grant insert                       on table public.meetups               to altair_api_writer;
grant update (status, cancelled_at) on table public.meetups              to altair_api_writer;
grant insert                       on table public.meetup_meeting_points to altair_api_writer;
grant insert, delete               on table public.rsvps                 to altair_api_writer;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- RLS policies
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------

-- users: yourself, and members of a group you share (attendee names).
create policy users_select_self_or_groupmates on public.users
  for select to authenticated, altair_api_writer
  using (id = (select app.current_user_id()) or app.shares_group_with(id));

-- groups: only groups you belong to ("my groups").
create policy groups_select_member on public.groups
  for select to authenticated, altair_api_writer
  using (app.is_group_member(id));

-- group_memberships: only your own rows.
create policy group_memberships_select_own on public.group_memberships
  for select to authenticated, altair_api_writer
  using (user_id = (select app.current_user_id()));

-- meetups: members of the group read (including cancelled ones).
create policy meetups_select_member on public.meetups
  for select to authenticated, altair_api_writer
  using (app.is_group_member(group_id));

-- meetups: a member creates in their own group, as themselves, scheduled,
-- starting in the future.
create policy meetups_insert_member on public.meetups
  for insert to altair_api_writer
  with check (
    created_by = (select app.current_user_id())
    and app.is_group_member(group_id)
    and status = 'scheduled'
    and cancelled_at is null
    and starts_at > now()
  );

-- meetups: only the creator updates (cancel). Column grant limits the
-- writer to status/cancelled_at; the trigger makes cancellation final.
create policy meetups_update_creator on public.meetups
  for update to altair_api_writer
  using (created_by = (select app.current_user_id()) and app.is_group_member(group_id))
  with check (created_by = (select app.current_user_id()));

-- meetup_meeting_points: creator and attendees only.
create policy meeting_points_select_creator_or_attendee on public.meetup_meeting_points
  for select to authenticated, altair_api_writer
  using (app.can_see_exact_meeting_point(meetup_id));

create policy meeting_points_insert_creator on public.meetup_meeting_points
  for insert to altair_api_writer
  with check (
    exists (
      select 1 from public.meetups m
       where m.id = meetup_id and m.created_by = (select app.current_user_id())
    )
  );

-- rsvps: members of the meetup's group see the attendee list.
create policy rsvps_select_member on public.rsvps
  for select to authenticated, altair_api_writer
  using (app.is_meetup_member(meetup_id));

-- rsvps: only for yourself, only in your own group.
create policy rsvps_insert_self on public.rsvps
  for insert to altair_api_writer
  with check (user_id = (select app.current_user_id()) and app.is_meetup_member(meetup_id));

-- rsvps: withdraw only your own (allowed after cancellation too).
create policy rsvps_delete_self on public.rsvps
  for delete to altair_api_writer
  using (user_id = (select app.current_user_id()));

-- =====================================================================
-- Access control: grants + row-level security for the meetup slice.
--
-- Two database roles act on behalf of a signed-in member:
--
--   authenticated       Supabase's role for requests carrying a member's
--                       JWT (the app, or the API server's read path).
--                       READ ONLY in this slice: no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
--                       grant on any table, so a write sent from the app
--                       straight to PostgREST is refused by the database.
--
--   altair_api_writer   NOLOGIN role that only the API server can assume
--                       (SET LOCAL ROLE inside a transaction, after it has
--                       verified the member's JWT and validated the body
--                       with the shared Zod schemas). PostgREST cannot
--                       switch to it: it is not granted to `authenticator`.
--                       It holds the minimum write grants, and RLS still
--                       applies to it as the member (creator-only cancel,
--                       own-RSVP-only, members-only create).
--
-- The member's identity comes from the `sub` claim of request.jwt.claims,
-- which PostgREST sets for `authenticated` and the API server sets for
-- `altair_api_writer` from the verified token. app.current_user_id() reads
-- it the same way auth.uid() does; it lives in `app` so the writer role
-- does not need privileges on Supabase's `auth` schema.
-- =====================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Writer role
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
do $$
begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = 'altair_api_writer') then
    create role altair_api_writer nologin noinherit;
  end if;
end
$$;

comment on role altair_api_writer is
  'Assumed only by the ALTAIR API server (SET LOCAL ROLE) for validated writes. Not reachable via PostgREST.';

-- The migration runs as the database owner (postgres), which is also the
-- role the API server connects as; it must be able to SET ROLE to the writer.
grant altair_api_writer to current_user;

grant usage on schema public to altair_api_writer;
grant usage on schema app to authenticated, altair_api_writer;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Identity + membership helpers
-- SECURITY DEFINER predicates read group_memberships without recursing
-- into its own RLS. Each answers a yes/no question about the caller only.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
create function app.current_user_id()
returns uuid
language sql
stable
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select coalesce(
    nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claim.sub', true), ''),
    nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), '')::jsonb ->> 'sub'
  )::uuid
$$;

create function app.is_group_member(p_group_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1 from public.group_memberships gm
     where gm.group_id = p_group_id
       and gm.user_id  = app.current_user_id()
  )
$$;

create function app.is_meetup_member(p_meetup_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1
      from public.meetups m
      join public.group_memberships gm on gm.group_id = m.group_id
     where m.id = p_meetup_id
       and gm.user_id = app.current_user_id()
  )
$$;

-- Creator or attendee, AND still a member of the meetup's group.
-- An RSVP grants exact access to that one meetup only.
create function app.can_see_exact_meeting_point(p_meetup_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1
      from public.meetups m
      join public.group_memberships gm
        on gm.group_id = m.group_id and gm.user_id = app.current_user_id()
     where m.id = p_meetup_id
       and (
         m.created_by = app.current_user_id()
         or exists (
           select 1 from public.rsvps r
            where r.meetup_id = m.id and r.user_id = app.current_user_id()
         )
       )
  )
$$;

create function app.shares_group_with(p_user_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1
      from public.group_memberships mine
      join public.group_memberships theirs on theirs.group_id = mine.group_id
     where mine.user_id   = app.current_user_id()
       and theirs.user_id = p_user_id
  )
$$;

revoke all on function app.current_user_id() from public;
revoke all on function app.is_group_member(uuid) from public;
revoke all on function app.is_meetup_member(uuid) from public;
revoke all on function app.can_see_exact_meeting_point(uuid) from public;
revoke all on function app.shares_group_with(uuid) from public;

grant execute on function app.current_user_id()                   to authenticated, altair_api_writer;
grant execute on function app.is_group_member(uuid)               to authenticated, altair_api_writer;
grant execute on function app.is_meetup_member(uuid)              to authenticated, altair_api_writer;
grant execute on function app.can_see_exact_meeting_point(uuid)   to authenticated, altair_api_writer;
grant execute on function app.shares_group_with(uuid)             to authenticated, altair_api_writer;

grant execute on function app.approximate_area(double precision, double precision) to altair_api_writer;
grant execute on function app.insert_meetup(uuid, uuid, text, timestamptz, text, double precision, double precision, uuid)
  to altair_api_writer;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table privileges. Supabase's default privileges grant ALL on new public
-- tables to anon and authenticated; start from nothing and add back only
-- what this slice needs. anon gets nothing at all.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
revoke all on table public.users                 from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on table public.groups                from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on table public.group_memberships     from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on table public.meetups               from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on table public.meetup_meeting_points from anon, authenticated;

grant select on table public.meetups               to authenticated, altair_api_writer;

  for select to authenticated, altair_api_writer

ALTAIR — OPTIONAL BONUS FEATURES

Implement the following optional bonus features after completing and verifying all mandatory requirements.

Implement a complete creator-only Edit Meetup feature.

Backend

Create an authenticated Edit Meetup endpoint.

Allow the creator to update:

Meetup title

Start time

Meeting-point name

Latitude

Longitude

Requirements:

Only the original meetup creator can edit.

Enforce creator-only authorization in PostgreSQL RLS or a secure database function.

Validate requests using the existing shared Zod schemas.

Reject invalid titles and coordinates.

When the start time changes, reject past or current times.

Reject editing cancelled meetups.

Never allow the client to change the creator ID or group ID.

Return appropriate errors without exposing unauthorized meetup information.

React Native

Create a professional Edit Meetup screen.

Include:

Existing values prefilled.

Editable title.

Date and time picker.

Meeting-point name.

Map-based location selection or coordinate inputs.

Save Changes button.

Loading and error states.

Success confirmation.

Only show the Edit action to the creator.

Automated Tests

Verify:

Creator can edit.

Other members cannot edit.

Outsiders cannot edit.

Cancelled meetups cannot be edited.

Invalid inputs are rejected.

Changed start times must be in the future.

Unauthorized direct database updates are denied.

BONUS B — REALTIME MAP WORK SAMPLE

Build a small, separate, demonstrable realtime map feature using Mapbox and Supabase Realtime.

This is a work sample, not a requirement to implement full production live-location sharing.

Core Functionality

Implement:

Mapbox map rendering.

Supabase Realtime broadcast channels.

Synthetic participant positions.

Animated participant avatars.

Position interpolation.

Viewport culling.

Realtime Position Updates

Use Supabase Realtime Broadcast to send simulated participant positions.

Include:

Participant ID

Latitude

Longitude

Timestamp

Sequence number where useful

Validate received payloads.

Handle malformed or stale messages safely.

Animated Avatars

Display participant avatars on the map.

When new positions arrive:

Animate smoothly between positions.

Avoid sudden marker jumps.

Interpolate coordinates between updates.

Handle delayed and out-of-order updates.

Avoid unnecessary React component rerenders.

Viewport Culling

Only render avatars within or near the visible map bounds.

Implement:

Visible-region filtering.

A small viewport margin.

Efficient updates when the map moves.

Reduced rendering work for offscreen participants.

Privacy and Security

Use synthetic position data for the demonstration.

Do not use real home locations.

Do not access users' private profile coordinates.

Do not expose precise positions to unauthorized users.

Use authenticated and appropriately authorized Realtime channels.

Do not enable real background location tracking.

Do not commit Mapbox access tokens or Supabase secrets.

Performance

Optimize:

Animation smoothness.

React Native rendering.

Network traffic.

Position update frequency.

Viewport calculations.

Battery usage.

Avoid unnecessary high-frequency broadcasts.

Documentation

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  checks:
    name: Lint, typecheck, offline tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run format:check
      - run: npm run typecheck
      # Shared contract + server unit tests + server API/DB tests on embedded
      # Postgres 17 (real migrations and seed) + React Native tests. No secrets.
      - run: npm run test:offline

  hosted:
    name: Hosted Supabase tests
    needs: checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Runs only when the repository has been given a test project's settings.
    if: ${{ vars.RUN_HOSTED_TESTS == 'true' }}
    env:
      SUPABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_URL }}
      SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY }}
      DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.DATABASE_URL }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run test:hosted

input.content:
# Altair: group meetups slice

A map-centred community feature for dog owners: members of small neighbourhood walking groups create
meetups at public places, RSVP, and see where to meet on a map. This repository is the slice the
First Epic workflow challenge asks for: **database (Supabase/Postgres + RLS), a Zod-validated write
layer, one shared contract, and an Expo React Native app** — built from the provided schema starter
and seed.

> Read [ENGINEERING_NOTES.md](ENGINEERING_NOTES.md) for the product decision (approximate area until
> RSVP), the security design and the trade-offs, and [QA_REPORT.md](QA_REPORT.md) for what was
> verified and how.

## What is in the slice

| Area | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Database | `meetups`, `meetup_meeting_points` (exact spot, split out so RLS can hide it), `rsvps`; RLS on every table; triggers for the domain rules (no RSVP to cancelled/started meetups, cancel is final). |
| Write layer | Fastify server. Every write (create, cancel, RSVP, withdraw, bonus edit) is validated with the shared Zod schemas, then runs **as the member** under RLS. The app cannot write to Supabase directly. |
| Shared contract | `packages/shared`: Zod 4 request/response schemas imported by the server **and** the app. |
| App | Expo (SDK 58) React Native: sign-in, group meetup list, create, detail with map + RSVP + creator-only cancel, bonus edit. |
| Privacy | Members who have not RSVP'd get an offset 400 m area, never the exact coordinates or place name. Home locations are not readable by any client-facing role. |
| Tests | 189 offline tests (embedded Postgres 17 running the real migrations + seed) and a hosted suite against real Supabase Auth/PostgREST/Postgres. |

## Architecture

```
 Expo app (React Native)                         Fastify API (Node 22)
 ┌───────────────────────────┐   HTTPS + JWT    ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ screens → hooks (React    │ ───────────────▶ │ routes: parse with shared Zod        │
 │ Query) → gateway ports    │                  │ services: business rules             │
 │ → ApiClient (Zod-parsed)  │ ◀─────────────── │ repositories (SQL) via UnitOfWork:   │
 └────────────┬──────────────┘  shared contract │   BEGIN; SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated│
              │ sign-in only                    │   | altair_api_writer;               │
              ▼                                 │   request.jwt.claims = {sub: member} │
       Supabase Auth  ◀──── token verification ─┴──────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                                                ▼
                                       Postgres (Supabase): RLS + column grants + triggers
```

- `authenticated` (the role a member's JWT maps to) is **read-only**: even with a valid session,
  the app cannot insert/update/delete anything through PostgREST.
- `altair_api_writer` is a `NOLOGIN` role only the API server can assume, after verifying the
  token and validating the body. RLS still applies to it as the member (creator-only cancel/edit,
  own-RSVP only, members-only create).

## Repository layout

```
supabase/
  migrations/20261001000000_starter.sql        provided starter, byte-for-byte
  migrations/20261029120000_meetups_and_rsvps.sql
  migrations/20261029120100_meetup_rules.sql    approximate area, insert function, triggers
  migrations/20261029120200_access_control.sql  roles, grants, RLS policies
  migrations/20261029140000_edit_meetup.sql     bonus: creator-only edit
  seed/part2_reference_meetups.sql              seed PART 2 adapted (idempotent)
packages/shared/        @altair/shared: Zod contract + tests
server/                 @altair/server: Fastify API
  src/domain            ports, types, pure rules (no framework imports)
  src/features/*        services (application) + routes (HTTP) per feature
  src/infrastructure    pg repositories, unit of work, Supabase token verifier
  src/http              app assembly, auth hook, error handler, validation
  test/unit|offline|hosted
mobile/                 @altair/mobile: Expo app
  src/core              ports, API client, Supabase auth adapter, DI context
  src/features/*        auth, groups, meetups (screens, components, hooks)
  src/ui                design system (theme, Button, Card, TextField, states)
  test/                 Jest + Testing Library
altair-feature-spec.html, altair-seed-data.sql, altair-schema-starter/   provided inputs, unchanged
```

## Prerequisites

- **Node.js ≥ 22.13** (Expo SDK 58 requires it) and npm ≥ 10.
- A **hosted Supabase project** (free tier is fine). No Docker needed.
- To run the app: an Android emulator (Android Studio) or a phone with **Expo Go for SDK 58**.
  iOS simulator also works on macOS. The web client is out of scope.

## Run from a clean checkout

### 1. Install

```bash
git clone <repo-url> altair && cd altair
npm ci
```

### 2. Configure

Create a Supabase project, then:

```bash
cp .env.example .env               # Windows PowerShell: Copy-Item .env.example .env
cp mobile/.env.example mobile/.env
```

| Variable | Where to find it |
| --- | --- |
| `SUPABASE_URL` | Project Settings → Data API → Project URL |
| `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | Project Settings → API Keys → publishable / `anon` key (**not** the service-role/secret key; nothing here needs it) |
| `DATABASE_URL` | **Connect** → *Session pooler* connection string, with your database password |
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` (mobile/.env) | Same URL and anon key; `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` = where the phone/emulator reaches the API (see below) |

Both `.env` files are git-ignored. Supabase Auth needs no extra configuration: the email provider
is on by default and the seed marks the accounts as confirmed.

### 3. Database: migrations, then seed (exactly once each)

The starter is the **first migration**, so it is applied by the Supabase CLI together with ours.
Do **not** also paste it into the SQL editor.

```bash
npm run db:push -- --dry-run   # shows the 5 migrations that would be applied
npm run db:push                # = npx supabase db push --db-url $DATABASE_URL
```

Then, in the Supabase dashboard → **SQL Editor** (runs as the database owner, which the seed needs):

1. Paste and run **`altair-seed-data.sql`** (the provided file, unchanged: PART 1 accounts,
   profiles, groups, memberships; PART 2 is commented out in it).
2. Paste and run **`supabase/seed/part2_reference_meetups.sql`** (PART 2 adapted to this schema).

Check that a seed account can sign in (prints an access token):

```bash
curl -s "$SUPABASE_URL/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password" -H "apikey: $SUPABASE_ANON_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email":"sam@example.test","password":"altair-fixture-pass"}'
```

To restore the three reference meetups later (fresh start times, seed RSVPs; nothing else is
touched): `npm run db:reset-reference`.

### 4. API server

```bash
npm run server          # http://localhost:4000/health → {"status":"ok"}
```

### 5. App

```bash
npm run mobile          # Expo dev server; press "a" for the Android emulator, or scan the QR code with Expo Go
```

`EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` must be reachable **from the device**:

| Where the app runs | API URL |
| --- | --- |
| Android emulator | `http://10.0.2.2:4000` |
| iOS simulator | `http://127.0.0.1:4000` |
| Physical phone (Expo Go) | `http://<your computer's LAN IP>:4000` (same Wi-Fi; allow port 4000 in the firewall) |

### 6. Tests

```bash
npm run test:offline   # no network, no credentials: shared + server (unit, API, DB on embedded Postgres 17) + mobile
npm run test:hosted    # against your Supabase project (needs .env)
npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run format:check
```

The hosted suite signs in as the seed accounts, re-runs `part2_reference_meetups.sql` before each
test (only the three reference meetups are reset) and deletes meetups it created (titles start with
`[test]`). It never touches other data.

## Seed accounts

Password for every account: `altair-fixture-pass` (published fixture; development/testing only).

| Email | Groups | Role in the reference meetups |
| --- | --- | --- |
| avery@example.test | Maple Street Walkers | creator of "Saturday morning loop" |
| jordan@example.test | Maple Street Walkers | RSVP'd to Saturday; creator of "Weeknight short walk" |
| sam@example.test | Maple Street Walkers | member, no RSVP |
| riley@example.test | both groups | RSVP'd to Saturday only |
| morgan@example.test | Riverside Loop Walkers | creator of "Riverside sunrise walk" |
| casey@example.test | Riverside Loop Walkers | RSVP'd to Riverside sunrise |
| quinn@example.test | Riverside Loop Walkers | member, no RSVP |
| taylor@example.test | neither | outsider |

The seed coordinates are synthetic, around 40.0000 N, 100.0000 W; the real-world map labels there
have nothing to do with the fictional place names.

## API

All `/v1` routes require `Authorization: Bearer <Supabase access token>`. Errors always have the
shape `{ "error": { "code", "message", "issues"? } }`.

| Method & path | Purpose | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | liveness | public |
| `GET /v1/me/groups` | the caller's groups | |
| `GET /v1/groups/:groupId/meetups` | meetups, soonest first, cancelled included | 404 for non-members |
| `GET /v1/groups/:groupId/map` | map data for the group's meetups | per-meetup visibility |
| `GET /v1/meetups/:id` | detail + attendees + meeting point | 404 for outsiders |
| `GET /v1/meetups/:id/attendees` | attendee names | |
| `GET /v1/meetups/:id/map` | the meeting point this member may see | |
| `POST /v1/meetups` | create | 201; creator = session user |

meetups at public places, RSVP, and see where to meet on a map. This repository is the slice the
First Epic workflow challenge asks for: **database (Supabase/Postgres + RLS), a Zod-validated write

and seed.

> Read [ENGINEERING_NOTES.md](ENGINEERING_NOTES.md) for the product decision (approximate area until
> RSVP), the security design and the trade-offs, and [QA_REPORT.md](QA_REPORT.md) for what was
> verified and how.

## What is in the slice

| Area | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Database | `meetups`, `meetup_meeting_points` (exact spot, split out so RLS can hide it), `rsvps`; RLS on every table; triggers for the domain rules (no RSVP to cancelled/started meetups, cancel is final). |
| Write layer | Fastify server. Every write (create, cancel, RSVP, withdraw, bonus edit) is validated with the shared Zod schemas, then runs **as the member** under RLS. The app cannot write to Supabase directly. |
| Shared contract | `packages/shared`: Zod 4 request/response schemas imported by the server **and** the app. |
| App | Expo (SDK 58) React Native: sign-in, group meetup list, create, detail with map + RSVP + creator-only cancel, bonus edit. |

| Tests | 189 offline tests (embedded Postgres 17 running the real migrations + seed) and a hosted suite against real Supabase Auth/PostgREST/Postgres. |

## Architecture

```
 Expo app (React Native)                         Fastify API (Node 22)
 ┌───────────────────────────┐   HTTPS + JWT    ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ screens → hooks (React    │ ───────────────▶ │ routes: parse with shared Zod        │

  test/unit|offline|hosted

  src/core              ports, API client, Supabase auth adapter, DI context
  src/features/*        auth, groups, meetups (screens, components, hooks)
  src/ui                design system (theme, Button, Card, TextField, states)
  test/                 Jest + Testing Library

```

is on by default and the seed marks the accounts as confirmed.

# Engineering notes

## 1. The product decision: approximate area until RSVP

**Decision.** Members who have not RSVP'd see an approximate area (a 400 m circle whose centre is
offset from the spot) and a generic label instead of the place name. The creator and members who
RSVP'd see the exact point and its name. RSVPing updates the map immediately; withdrawing turns it
back into the area.

**Why, in terms of the people using the app.** A meetup post says *where a specific neighbour
will be, at a specific time, usually early morning or evening, often alone with a dog*. Walking
groups are "a handful to a few dozen neighbours" and membership is loose (people join, move,
lose interest), so "everyone in the group" is a wider and less known audience than "the people
who said they are coming". The decision a non-attendee actually has to make, *is this walk near
me and when*, only needs the area and the time. The exact gathering spot is needed only by the
people who will walk there, and an RSVP is a light, visible commitment (attendees are listed by
name), which gives the organiser accountability for who knows the spot. The cost is one tap
before you see the pin; the area is precise enough to decide whether to tap.

**How the area is computed (in the database, `app.approximate_area`).**

- Centre = exact point moved **120–280 m in a random direction**; radius **400 m**. The exact
  point is always inside the circle (offset < radius), so the area is honest.
- **Computed once at creation and stored**, never re-randomised per request: repeated reads can't
  be averaged back to the spot. (When the creator moves the point with the bonus edit, a new area
  is computed around the new point.)
- **Random per meetup**, not a fixed shift and not a grid: learning one meetup's exact point by
  RSVPing tells you nothing about another meetup's offset. A grid snap was rejected because a spot

  RSVPing tells you nothing about another meetup's offset. A grid snap was rejected because a spot
  near a cell centre gives an area centred almost on the spot.
- The **place name never leaves the server** before RSVP; the app shows its own label.

**Where it is enforced.** The exact point lives in its own table, `meetup_meeting_points`, whose
RLS policy admits only the creator and attendees who are still group members
(`app.can_see_exact_meeting_point`). RLS is per row, not per column, so the split is what lets the
database alone withhold it. The `meetups` row a member can read contains only the area. The service
layer applies a second, independent check (`meetingPointFor`), and every response is parsed
through the shared Zod schema, which drops anything not in the contract.

## 2. Architecture

| Layer | Server | App |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Presentation | `http/` (Fastify app, auth hook, error handler), `features/*/…routes.ts` | `features/*/screens`, `components`, `ui/` |
| Application | `features/*/…service.ts` (business rules, no SQL) | `features/*/hooks.ts` (React Query) |
| Domain / ports | `domain/` (types, ports, pure rules, errors) | `core/ports.ts` |
| Infrastructure | `infrastructure/` (pg repositories, unit of work, Supabase token verifier) | `core/api`, `core/auth` (Supabase), composition in `App.tsx` |
| Contract | `packages/shared` (imported by both) | |

Dependencies point inward: routes → services → ports ← repositories. `index.ts` (server) and
`App.tsx` (app) are the only composition roots. That is what lets the same services run against
fakes (unit tests), embedded Postgres (offline tests) and hosted Supabase (hosted tests), and lets
the app screens be tested with fake gateways.

**Kept deliberately small:** one Fastify process, no DI container, no ORM, no event bus, no
generic repository base class. Plain SQL in three repositories is easier to review against RLS
than an ORM's generated queries.

### Reads go through the API too

Reads may legally go straight to PostgREST under RLS, and the database is built so that would be
safe (the hosted tests prove it). I still route reads through the API so the app consumes **one
contract** for everything (a meetup's `viewer` flags and `meetingPoint` union are computed in one
place) and so a schema change can't silently break the app.

## 3. Security approach

- **Writes only through the API.** `authenticated` has `SELECT` only; no insert/update/delete
  grant on any table and no execute on the `app` functions (and `app` is not an exposed API
  schema). Writes run as `altair_api_writer`, a `NOLOGIN` role that PostgREST cannot switch to.
  The API binds the verified member to the transaction with `SET LOCAL ROLE` and a
  transaction-local `request.jwt.claims`, so pooled connections never leak identity between
  requests.
- **RLS on everything**, including writes: creator-only cancel/edit, RSVP/withdraw only for
  yourself, create only in your own group and only as yourself. The server's checks give good error
  messages; the database is the enforcement.
- **Home location**: `users` has a *column-level* grant (`id, display_name`) for client-facing
  roles. `select home_lat …` and `select * from users` fail with "permission denied" even for your
  own row. No query in the server selects anything else from `users`.
- **Domain rules in triggers** (they hold for every writer, including the owner): no RSVP to a
  cancelled or started meetup, RSVP user must be a group member, cancellation is final, identity
  columns immutable. The RSVP trigger locks the meetup row `FOR SHARE`, which serialises it against
  a concurrent cancel (hosted test: an RSVP blocked behind an uncommitted cancel is rejected once
  the cancel commits).
- **No information leaks in errors.** Outsiders get the same `404 Meetup not found` for a real
  meetup as for a random id (tested byte-for-byte). The RSVP trigger checks membership *before*
  status, so an outsider can't probe whether a meetup is cancelled. Unknown errors become a generic
  500; SQL and stack traces are only logged server-side. The `Authorization` header is redacted
  from logs.
- **Never trust the client**: request schemas are strict (an extra `createdBy`, `groupId` on edit,
  or a body on RSVP is a 400). The creator is always `app.current_user_id()` from the verified
  token.
- **Service-role key**: not used anywhere. It is not needed and is not in any `.env` template.

### Privileged functions and their properties

| Function | Security | Why it is safe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app.is_group_member`, `is_meetup_member`, `can_see_exact_meeting_point`, `shares_group_with` | DEFINER, `search_path=''` | Read `group_memberships` without recursing into its RLS; answer yes/no about the **caller** only. |
| `app.guard_rsvp_insert` (trigger) | DEFINER | Locks the meetup row regardless of the caller's RLS view; returns nothing but an error code; checks membership first. |
| `app.on_meeting_point_update` (trigger, bonus) | DEFINER | Only fires for rows the caller's RLS already allowed them to update; recomputes the area (owner-only columns). |
| `app.insert_meetup` | INVOKER | Runs under the writer's RLS; the seed calls it as owner. |

## 4. Trade-offs and what I'd change for production

- The API connects with the database owner's credentials and *drops* privileges per transaction.
  For production I'd create a dedicated `LOGIN` role that is a member of only `authenticated` and
  `altair_api_writer`, so a compromised API process can't bypass RLS.
- Token verification calls Supabase Auth (`getUser`) per request: simple, and correct for revoked
  sessions and for both legacy and asymmetric signing keys. At scale I'd verify locally against
  the project's JWKS and cache.
- The approximate area is a random draw stored per meetup. In very sparse areas a 400 m circle may
  contain only one plausible public place; the product should eventually size areas by place
  density, not a constant.
- `random()` (not a CSPRNG) chooses the offset. An attacker can't observe the generator, and the
  value is drawn once, so this is adequate; `gen_random_bytes` would be the stricter choice.
- "Started" is `starts_at <= now()` in the database clock (also used for `canRsvp`), so the app
  and the trigger never disagree.

## 5. One thing I would refuse to build first

**Live location sharing of members during walks** (the brief's optional realtime map, as a real
feature). For a dog-walking group, a walk usually *starts at someone's front door*, so a live
track leaks the very home location this spec makes private, plus routines and times when a person
is out. I would not build it until there is per-walk opt-in, sharing that starts only inside a
geofence around the public meeting point and stops automatically, no retention of tracks, and
visibility limited to attendees of that walk. (That is how the bonus work sample, if built, is
scoped: synthetic positions only, private channels restricted to attendees.)

## 6. What I would push back on in the spec

1. **No end time or duration.** "Started" is the only cut-off, so a meetup is never "over"; lists
   grow forever and the app can't separate *upcoming* from *past*. I'd add a duration (or end
   time) and default the list to upcoming.
2. **Editing the place after people RSVP'd** (bonus) silently changes their plans. Attendees
   should be told, and possibly asked to re-confirm; notifications are out of scope, so today they
   only find out by opening the meetup.
3. **Cancellation is invisible to attendees** for the same reason. A cancelled walk at 7 am that
   nobody hears about is a real failure mode; this is the first notification I'd ship.
4. **Creators who leave the group.** RLS requires membership, so a creator who leaves can no
   longer cancel and the meetup is orphaned. The spec needs an owner-transfer or group-admin rule.
5. **The attendee list is visible before RSVP.** Fine inside a small group, but combined with time
   and area it says who will be where; worth a conscious decision rather than a default.
6. **A fixed 300 m minimum** protects little in dense areas and may still identify the spot in
   sparse ones (see trade-offs). The requirement should be about ambiguity (number of plausible
   places), not metres.

## 7. Assumptions

- A member may RSVP to their own meetup (they're a member; the creator already sees the exact
  point, so it only adds them to the attendee list).
- RSVPing twice returns 200 and leaves one RSVP, even if the meetup has since been cancelled or
  started (the existing RSVP simply stands). Withdrawing without an RSVP is a 200 no-op.
- Cancelling an already-cancelled meetup is a 200 no-op. A creator may cancel a meetup that has
  started.
- A member who leaves a group loses access to its meetups, including exact points they had via
  RSVP.
- Deleted users appear as "Former member".

## 8. If the starter was already applied

The Supabase CLI records applied migrations in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. If the
starter was pasted into the SQL editor instead, `db push` will try to apply
`20261001000000_starter.sql` again and fail on "relation already exists". Do not drop anything:
mark only the starter as applied, then push the rest:

```bash
npx supabase migration repair --db-url "$DATABASE_URL" --status applied 20261001000000
npm run db:push
```

## 9. How this was built (AI-assisted)

The code, SQL, tests and documents in this repository were written by an AI coding agent
(Claude Code) under the developer's direction, in one session whose exported log accompanies the
submission. The agent ran every command shown in QA_REPORT.md. What it caught and corrected along
the way, from that log:

- **npm 10 crash** (`edgesOut` of null) during the first install: switched the portable Node's npm
  to 11. The agent's first attempt installed npm 11 into the *user-global* prefix, which changed
  the machine's default npm; it noticed, removed exactly the files it had added, and installed
  npm 11 into the project's ignored `.tools/` instead.
- **Testing Library 14 made `render` and `fireEvent` async**: 18 of 23 app tests failed with
  "render has not been called". Fixed by awaiting them, and added a type-aware
  `no-floating-promises` lint rule for the app tests (then proved the rule fires).
- **Rules-of-hooks bug** in the detail screen (a hook called after early returns), spotted during
  writing and fixed before the first run.
- **Mutation checks** of the privacy tests: weakening the exact-point RLS policy and the service's
  entitlement check made 12 tests fail; weakening the bonus edit policy made the edit test fail.
  During the second check the restore step used `git checkout` on a then-untracked file, which
  silently did nothing; the agent detected the leftover `using (true)`, restored the policy by
  hand, and verified no permissive policy remains.
- A test that asserted "the writer role cannot change a title" became wrong by design once the
  edit bonus granted that column; it was rewritten to assert what must remain impossible
  (changing group or creator).
- A meetup whose creator's profile is not visible (left the group) would have disappeared from
  lists with an inner join; the queries use a left join and "Former member".
